walkthroughs.body_html:
Judaism Option — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Judaism Option brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Judaism Option.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How many commandments are in the Torah?
Where was the Sinai Covenant made?
options: Egypt
Mt Sinai
Canaan
Babylon

mcqs.q: Why do Jews not accept Jesus as the Messiah?
options: The Torah is a single scroll containing every Jewish text.
Because Jews believe Jesus never existed.
Because the Jewish Messiah is expected to bring peace, rebuild the Temple and restore Israel — events the Jewish tradition holds Jesus did not accomplish.
Because Jesus was crucified, and the Messiah cannot die.
The Torah is the same as the Book of Genesis.
Because Jesus was crucified, and the Messiah cannot die.
The Torah is a single scroll containing every Jewish text.
The first five books of the Hebrew Bible (Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy) — traditionally attributed to Moses and containing law, narrative and covenant.

mcqs.q: What does the Abrahamic covenant in Judaism involve?
options: The Torah is a single scroll containing every Jewish text.
God's promise to Abraham of land, descendants and blessing, in return for faithfulness — the foundational covenant marking Jews as a covenant people with responsibilities, not privileges.
Being 'chosen' means Jews believe they are superior to other peoples.
The covenant means Jews must not interact with non-Jews.
